classification.difficultyReason: Choose the central coefficient, use symmetry to obtain squared coefficients with alternating signs, and match its degree to the x-squared expansion on the right.

content.prompt:
By considering $(1+x)^{2n}(1-x)^{2n}=(1-x^2)^{2n}$, equate an appropriate $x^r$ to show that
$$\binom{2n}0^2-\binom{2n}1^2+\binom{2n}2^2-\binom{2n}3^2+\cdots+\binom{2n}{2n}^2$$
is equal to $\displaystyle(-1)^n\binom{2n}n$.

answer.worked:
Equate the coefficients of $x^{2n}$. On the left, choose $x^{2n-j}$ from $(1+x)^{2n}$ and $x^j$ from $(1-x)^{2n}$. On the right, the required term uses $(-x^2)^n$:
$$\begin{align*}
\sum_{j=0}^{2n}(-1)^j\binom{2n}{2n-j}\binom{2n}j
&=(-1)^n\binom{2n}n.
\end{align*}$$
Using $\binom{2n}{2n-j}=\binom{2n}j$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
\sum_{j=0}^{2n}(-1)^j\binom{2n}j^2
&=(-1)^n\binom{2n}n.
\end{align*}$$
The left-hand side is the required alternating sum.
